chunks: What the Sheikh — may Allah the Exalted support him — related to me: he said: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn al-Hasan informed me, from his father, from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn 'Ali ibn Mahbub, from Ahmad al-Barqi, from al-Nawfali, from al-Sakuni, from Ja'far, from his father, from his forefathers — peace be upon them all — who said:
The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and his family, forbade a man from facing the sun and the moon with his private parts while urinating.

key_terms.نَهَى: forbade, issued a prohibition (nahy, a legal interdiction)
key_terms.يَبُولُ: while urinating, in the act of urination
key_terms.يَسْتَقْبِلَ: face toward, turn oneself to, direct at

ai.seo_question: Did the Prophet Muhammad forbid a man from facing the sun or moon with his private parts while urinating?
ai.summary: This hadith transmits a legal ruling narrated through Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq (AS) from his forefathers (AS): the Prophet Muhammad (SAWW) forbade a man from directing his private parts toward the sun or the moon while urinating. The ruling belongs to the adab (proper conduct) of relieving oneself and is situated in the chapter on acts that necessitate ritual purification (tahara); it reflects prophetic reverence for the celestial signs of Allah's creation.
